title: Singleton factorization under a product law
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of its summary $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. Suppose the conditional law of the special-bit pair on the fiber $Z=z$ equals the product of the conditional laws of the individual special bits. Then, for every $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$, the real mass of the pair law at $\{b\}$ equals the product of the real masses of the two marginal laws at $\{b_1\}$ and $\{b_2\}$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic length-$n$ disjointness protocol
the conditional special-pair law equals the product of the two conditional marginal laws
replaced:
Fix a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$ and an achievable
value $z$ of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$. Write $\mu$ for the conditional
law of the special-coordinate bit-pair on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$, and $\mu_X$, $\mu_Y$
for the conditional laws on that same fiber of Alice's bit and of Bob's bit at the
special coordinate, all measures on Boolean values. Suppose the joint law factors as the
product of its marginals, $\mu = \mu_X \otimes \mu_Y$. Then for every pair of bits $b =
(b_1, b_2) \in \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Bool}$, the real-valued mass assigned to the
singleton is the product of the marginal masses, \[ \mu(\{b\}) = \mu_X(\{b_1\}) \cdot
\mu_Y(\{b_2\}). \]
